_description: Known divergences between the Tonats'oyts (Grabar) citation numbering the engine emits and the target versification used to retrieve text. First pass: only whole-range endpoint shifts are corrected; every other divergence is flagged and served unchanged. Detection is best-effort and NOT exhaustive.
_keying: Each record is keyed on the tuple (book, start_chapter, start_verse, end_chapter, end_verse) exactly as it appears in ReadingsRefs -- never on the citation string, which a composite citation shares across two refs of which only one is flagged.
_evidence: Every record was confirmed by reading the Armenian text against the English text, NOT by trusting an automated label: an unannotated arak29 row is not proof of identity (Hosea 14 is annotation-free and shifted by one). Two Armenian witnesses were compared for every record -- the Grabar 1895 Constantinople edition (arak29.org, which carries an inline KJV concordance) and Nor Ejmiatsin 1994 -- because they do not always agree, and where they disagree NE is the better witness for what a Tonats'oyts citation means. Luke 8.22-56, Luke 8.49-56 and Mark 4.35-41 look divergent in the 1895 edition and are plain identity in NE; they carry no record for that reason.

_survey: A sweep of all 1126 distinct served sub-references (2001-2027) against KJV chapter lengths, both Armenian witnesses' chapter inventories, and arak29's explicit KJV annotations raised 113 candidates. The 23 carrying a hard signal (an explicit annotation, an address absent from a witness, or a stated missing verse) were each resolved by reading the text; the resolutions are the records below. The remaining ~84 differ only in chapter verse-count and are UNRESOLVED -- they need the scholarly review this pass defers. A reading with no record here is unflagged, not verified.
